[NMET.3.3] `ds_metric_kind_t` has **three** members —
`DS_METRIC_COUNTER`, `DS_METRIC_GAUGE` and
`DS_METRIC_HISTOGRAM` ([NCBK.3.2]) — and the kind is
what tells a receiver how to fold `value`: a counter
contributes an increment, a gauge replaces the previous
reading, a histogram is one observation.

A histogram emit therefore identifies itself as one, and
a receiver does not have to infer it from the metric's
name. What the name and the declared bucket schema
([NMET.2.4]) still carry is how to *interpret* the
observation — which bucket set it belongs to, and in
what unit — because the engine emits raw observations
and never pre-buckets ([NMET.2.4.2]).
